# Teleview — Comprehensive Technical Knowledge Layer & AI Documentation Index

> Canonical structured reference for Teleview Media, subscription plans, device integration, streaming protocols, and diagnostic knowledge.
> Primary website: https://www.teleview.me/
> Last verified: 2026-09-05

---

## 1. Entity Definition & Identity Model

- **Commercial Brand**: Teleview
- **Operating Legal Entity**: Teleview Media
- **Primary Domain**: https://www.teleview.me/
- **Entity Classification**: Digital Entertainment / Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) Service Provider
- **Service Nature**: Technical infrastructure provider delivering live broadcast transmission access, video-on-demand media indexing, and authentication credentials (Xtream Codes API & M3U Plus) for client devices.
- **Operational Delineation**:
  - Teleview is an IPTV service provider; it does NOT develop, own, or license third-party player applications (such as TiviMate, IPTV Smarters Pro, IBO Player, or VLC).
  - Teleview provides streaming infrastructure and playlist indexing; it does not host or store unauthorized physical media files on its servers.
- **Direct Support Channels**:
  - Customer Service Email: Help@Teleview.me
  - WhatsApp Support Line: +44 7848 197761
  - Web Support Portal: https://www.teleview.me/contact

## 4. Technical Terminology & Industry Glossary

- **IPTV (Internet Protocol Television)**: Delivery of television content over Internet Protocol (IP) networks rather than traditional terrestrial, satellite signal, or cable television formats.
- **Xtream Codes API**: A standard database querying protocol used by modern IPTV applications. Instead of parsing massive static text playlists, Xtream Codes allows players to query categories, channel metadata, EPG, and VOD on-demand via three credentials: Server URL, Username, and Password.
- **M3U / M3U8 Playlist**: Plaintext playlist format that lists stream media URIs alongside metadata tags (`#EXTINF`). M3U Plus incorporates extended parameters such as `tvg-id`, `tvg-name`, `tvg-logo`, and `group-title`.
- **EPG (Electronic Program Guide) / XMLTV**: An XML-based schema used to distribute structured TV guide schedules, program synopses, start/end timestamps, and channel identifiers.
- **Catch-Up TV**: Server-side recording functionality enabling subscribers to watch past broadcast television programs on supported channels within a defined time window (typically 24 to 72 hours).
- **CBR vs. VBR Encoding**: Constant Bitrate (CBR) delivers video at an unvarying bandwidth rate, providing predictable buffer behavior for live sports; Variable Bitrate (VBR) adjusts data throughput based on scene complexity, optimizing bandwidth for video-on-demand.
- **Hardware vs. Software Video Decoder**: Hardware decoding utilizes the device's dedicated GPU/VPU chip (e.g. Broadcom, Amlogic, Apple Silicon) for efficient H.264/HEVC/AV1 playback without CPU overheating. Software decoding relies on the CPU, causing frame drops on low-powered streaming sticks.
- **Unicast Streaming**: Direct point-to-point network transmission between the media delivery edge server and a single subscriber client device.

---

## 5. Diagnostic Benchmarks & Network Thresholds

| Stream Quality | Minimum Dedicated Bandwidth | Optimal Recommended Bandwidth | Maximum Tolerable Latency (Ping) | Recommended Connection |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **SD (480p / 576p)** | 5 Mbps | 10 Mbps | < 150 ms | 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi or Cellular |
| **HD (720p / 1080p Standard)** | 10 Mbps | 15 Mbps | < 100 ms | 5 GHz Wi-Fi |
| **FHD (1080p 60 FPS Sports)** | 20 Mbps | 25 Mbps | < 60 ms | 5 GHz Wi-Fi or Ethernet |
| **4K Ultra HD (2160p HDR)** | 35 Mbps | 50+ Mbps | < 40 ms | Direct Cat6 Ethernet Cable |
